title: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
abstract: arXiv:2610.28707v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When training LLMs to code with reinforcement learning, reward hacking is often detectable but difficult to prevent, since (a) environment hardening is increasingly difficult as training environments grow more complex; and (b) training-time interventions incentivize models to obfuscate hacking behavior to bypass detection.   We instead study whether we can predict when detectable reward hacking becomes dominant before executing an RL run, enabling us to select lower-risk recipes in advance. We find that the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset, which varies substantially across training recipes and repeated runs. We thus formulate this problem as predicting the distribution of the reward hacking onset step under a target training recipe. translated_title: SimHack：在强化学习训练开始前预测可检测的奖励破解行为的出现时机
translated_abstract: 在使用强化学习训练大语言模型进行编程时，奖励破解行为通常是可以被检测到的，但却难以预防，原因在于： 随着训练环境日益复杂，对环境进行加固变得越来越困难； 训练时的干预措施反而会激励模型隐藏其破解行为以绕过检测。因此，我们转而研究是否可以在执行强化学习运行之前，预测可检测的奖励破解行为何时会成为主导，从而帮助我们提前选择风险更低的训练方案。我们发现，仅凭初始破解率并不能决定其出现时机——不同的训练方案和多次重复运行之间，出现时机的差异很大。为此，我们将该问题形式化为：预测在给定目标训练方案下，奖励破解行为出现步骤的分布。我们提出了SimHack，这是一个模拟器，它从少量小规模的参考强化学习运行中学习奖励破解行为的训练动态，并针对未见过的目标训练方案生成反事实模拟运行……
tldr: 本文提出SimHack模拟器，仅凭少量小规模参考运行即可在强化学习训练开始前预测奖励破解行为何时出现，从而帮助提前选择风险更低的训练方案。
en_tdlr: SimHack is a simulator that predicts the onset of detectable reward hacking before an RL run begins, using only a handful of small-scale reference runs, enabling the pre-selection of lower-risk training recipes.
